title: Gail and the Princess Who Forgot to Smile

en: Gail follows a path to a quiet castle.
A little sigh comes through an open window.
She stops to listen.
Princess Ella sits beside a tall window.
Outside, children are playing together.
Gail steps inside and wonders why Ella looks so quiet.
The room is full of gifts, blocks, and toys.
Yet Ella has no friend beside her.
A room full of things can still feel lonely.
Gail wants to help, so she plans a surprise.
Perhaps a wonderful tower will make Ella smile.
She reaches for a box of blocks.
Gail carefully builds a tall tower with the blocks.
Ella reaches out and asks to help.
“Wait until it is finished!” says Gail, keeping her surprise a secret.
The tall tower wobbles and falls across the rug.
Gail looks disappointed.
Ella picks up a block, hoping they can rebuild it together.
Gail tries bubbles, music, and a funny paper hat.
She is so busy making surprises that she forgets to ask Ella.
The room becomes noisy.
Ella covers her ears and quietly asks Gail to stop.
Gail puts down the paper hat.
At last, the room is quiet enough to listen.
Gail sits down at Ella’s side instead of making another surprise.
“What would you like to do?” she asks.
Then she waits and listens to her friend.
Ella points to the children beyond the window.
“I do not need another gift. I want a friend to play with.”
Gail smiles. “Let us choose something together.”
With her caregiver’s permission, Ella chooses a trip to the market.
Gail brings a basket, and the caregiver comes with them.
Together, they walk out through the castle gate.
At the market, an orange rolls away from a fruit stall.
Ella spots it and runs a few steps to help.
Gail follows while their caregiver waits nearby.
Ella picks up the oranges while Gail holds the basket.
They return the fruit to the grateful seller.
Working together feels better than watching a surprise.
In the open square, Gail takes out a paper pinwheel.
She and Ella take turns running while their caregiver watches.
The little paper wings spin as the friends share.
Suddenly, rain patters across the square.
The friends and their caregiver hurry under an awning.
Their soggy paper pinwheel will no longer turn.
Ella has an idea for repairing the pinwheel.
Gail holds the paper while Ella folds it carefully.
They straighten the wings together until it turns again.
With a spare piece of paper, Ella folds a funny hat for Gail.
Gail puts it on, but one corner slips down.
It tickles the tip of her nose.
Gail gives a tiny sneeze, and the crooked hat bounces.
Ella begins to laugh, and Gail laughs too.
Nobody planned this smile; it grew from their shared fun.
Back at the castle, two children join Gail and Ella on the rug.
They share the blocks and build a little castle together.
Ella adds a piece of her own this time.
Ella pulls out a chair and saves a place beside her.
“Will you come back tomorrow?” she asks her new friend.
Side by side, we laugh and play. A little friendship lights the day.
